channel.title: verify402 — notes from before the signature
channel.description: Scope, receipts, and field notes from building a pre-signing gate for agent payments.

item.title: What x402's 402s actually look like
item.description: 300 most-called public x402 endpoints, one read-only probe each: Base, canonical USDC, five-minute authorizations — and the 57 that ask for an hour.

item.title: What verify402-mcp 1.1.0 ships
item.description: Two free tools, seller-signed terms binding, a payment-token registry, durable /usage counters — and the things that did not change.

item.title: Check an x402 endpoint before you pay it
item.description: A 402 is a price tag, not a receipt. The six fields that decide what you sign, and a free way to check any endpoint without a wallet.

item.title: Put a pre-signing gate in an MCP agent in 15 minutes
item.description: Three free tools, one config block, and one hook that makes the signature unreachable until the receipt verifies.

item.title: What a pre-signing gate can check — and what it can't
item.description: The checklist a gate can run on an agent payment or approval, and the things it must say it does not know.

item.title: A receipt is not a guarantee. It's a falsifiable record.
item.description: What a preflight receipt proves, what it does not, and why intent binding matters more than a green icon.

item.title: Three payment intents your agent should never sign unchecked
item.description: An unlimited approval, an x402 offer that does not match the resource, and a swap with no floor. The signature is valid; the intent is not.
